To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fiber reinforced concrete has lower slump, air content, and setting times; it undergoes less shrinkage but more creep; and its air-void characteristics indicate that it has lower specific surface, and it has a lower number of chord-intersects in the 0-to-0.002-in (0 to 5-mm) range.
steel fiber reinforced concrete has a lower slump and air-contents and a higher rate of loss of slump and air-content than the corresponding plain concrete mixtures.
fiber reinforced concrete is less workable and more stiff than plain concrete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a fiber reinforced concrete mixture with a high workability, a high strength, and a low permeability.

the behavior of steel-fiber concrete under short-term loading conditions, and the results indicate that the behavior of steel fibers in the concrete is similar to that of steel fibers in a cement paste.
the development of a high-performance fiber concrete with a cement content of 611 lb/yd sup3 (363 kg/m sup 2) and an air-void system that can withstand freeze-thaw cycles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fiber reinforcement does not affect the setting times, but it affects the slump and air content.
the presence of fiber does not significantly affect the properties of fresh concrete, and the effect is not very pronounced in the long term.
fiber concrete has a higher degree of workability and a lower degree of air entrainment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of steel fibers in concrete does not affect its setting times, but it reduces its workability and air content.
steel fiber reinforcement has a beneficial effect on the properties of high-strength concrete, and the effect of fibers is not as detrimental as in lower strength concretes.
fiber reinforced concrete has slightly lower shrinkage, slightly lower creep, slightly higher air content loss, and slightly higher slump loss than plain concrete.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of fiber reinforced concrete are different from those of plain concrete.
fiber concrete is a good alternative to plain concrete.
the fiber concrete is more sensitive to changes in the mixture proportions.
